leapfrogs.title: H1 derived Kato -> complex L''
leapfrogs.known_baseline: Known algebraic rank-four points; BKS derived norm in augmentation I^3 if Theorem 1.3 conditions hold. Published BKS Proposition 4.4 concerns first layers Q_n of cyclotomic Z11-extension, with standing Sha(E/Q)[11∞] finiteness; it does not prove complex L'' vanishing.
leapfrogs.missing_arrow: Augmentation filtration I^3 of derived Kato class in H1 ⊗ Z11[G] is not a statement about the complex Taylor coefficient.
leapfrogs.hypothetical_bridge: Find a well-defined comparison map from independently computed derived classes to the complex L'' coefficient, with explicit noncircular hypotheses and injectivity on the tested quotient.
leapfrogs.if_then_statement: IF such a comparison exists and maps a rigorously verified annihilated class to L'' without circular assumptions, THEN L''(E,1)=0.
leapfrogs.would_unlock: A proof of the missing comparison and verified hypotheses would rule out analytic rank two for E.
leapfrogs.unverified_dependencies: Burns–Kurihara–Sano Theorem 1.3 assumes 11-primary Sha(E/F) finite among other requirements; the leading-term formula is conjectural and involves analytic input. Candidate F=Q(zeta_23)^+ has not established Sha(E/F)[11^infinity] finiteness. Exact input checks and standard Tate/unipotent arguments now address the local torsion and SL2(Z11)-image conditions for F=Q(zeta23)^+, pending expert review, but Sha(E/F)[11^infinity] remains unproved. Cyclotomic BKS Proposition 4.4 is conditional on standing Sha(E/Q)[11∞] finiteness; its Iwasawa graded coefficient is not known and no reciprocity to complex L'' is constructed.
leapfrogs.negative_control: The I^3 inclusion also holds in a toy with complex germ t^2, so it does not force a complex zero without a bridge. The ordinary trace of C11 reduces mod11 to T^10 despite nonzero integral augmentation 11, and an infinite class 11*T^3 vanishes in first I1³/I1⁴ but not second I2³/I2⁴.
leapfrogs.next_decisive_test: Use canonical degree-11 cyclotomic Q1 subset Q(zeta_121), not only Q(zeta23)^+, and test integral I1³/I1⁴ data with Q2 compatibility. First identify actual cohomological derived zeta element and determine whether its leading graded class is computationally accessible without Sha(E/Q)[11∞] finiteness.
leapfrogs.kill_criterion: Stop if the only accessible relation is an augmentation divisibility statement or depends on rank equality as a hypothesis.
leapfrogs.not_unlocked: No demonstrated theorem establishing L''(E,1)=0, analytic rank four, Sha finiteness, or the full BSD leading coefficient.

leapfrogs.title: H2 Bockstein mixed regulator -> complex L''
leapfrogs.known_baseline: Known anticyclotomic p-adic height theory and one-prime modified Selmer constructions.
leapfrogs.missing_arrow: No proven comparison in this project transports a p-adic height radical to the original complex L'' coefficient.
leapfrogs.hypothetical_bridge: Construct a comparison law between the actual one-prime modified Selmer complex and an analytically relevant complex regulator, fully stating characters and local splittings.
leapfrogs.if_then_statement: IF a valid comparison identifies a rigorously zero derived regulator with L'' and is nondegenerate, THEN L''=0.
leapfrogs.would_unlock: A different route via globally-defined Selmer-complex data could bypass raw analytic zero testing.
leapfrogs.unverified_dependencies: One-place modified Selmer must not be replaced by the two-place logarithm kernel; related published results may require Sha finiteness. Session 13 sourced a rank-independent *height computation* in BCLMN (2016), but no sigma-series or denominator-ideal calculation for [36]Ai is yet available. Anticyclotomic character coefficients alone cannot determine heights. The exact division polynomial and minimal model calculations now yield C-0011 provisional mod11 heights, but an independent p-adic sigma / height library and paper normalization audit are not yet complete; full higher derived regulator and complex L'' comparison remain unknown. Despite ten direct affine points, exact norm-gcd primitivity and six pair controls, the Mazur–Tate p-adic sigma power series and BCLMN global character formula are shared assumptions pending independent Sage/Magma height library review.
leapfrogs.negative_control: Identical dimensions of two kernel spaces may conceal different subspaces; explicit toy counterpairing shows the failure. Additional scale trap: a toy vector (0,1,0,0) times 11^3 makes all wedge residues vanish mod 11^3 while primitive normalization immediately rejects projective profile [1:0:2:9]. Session14 provisional genuine self-height vector (1,2,7,8) mod11 differs projectively from two-place local-log vector (1,0,2,9); the candidate L11 kernel-alignment is therefore conditionally *refuted*, pending a separate Sage/PARI global height check. Three naive denominator generators are nonprimitive by ideal norm factor 16, a specific bad-component false positive. Session 15 all six distinct Pi+Pj+R first-height values reproduce predicted sums and direct affine [36]Q norms show primitive global denominator ideals on ten inputs. This independently tests the global height arithmetic rather than merely the old 36/72 scalar homogeneity.
leapfrogs.next_decisive_test: Compute the BCLMN global 11-adic sigma series on the minimal model in an independently maintained Sage or Magma implementation, verify the exact first-digit height vector (1,2,7,8) with all local characters, and then obtain the 11-adic height functional to higher precision on the three-dimensional first-height radical (mod11 generators P2−2P1, P3−7P1, P4−8P1). Do not use two-prime local elliptic logarithm kernel as a derived-height replacement.
leapfrogs.kill_criterion: Park if no map with specified domain, codomain and analytic normalization can be stated.
leapfrogs.not_unlocked: No demonstrated theorem establishing L''(E,1)=0, analytic rank four, Sha finiteness, or the full BSD leading coefficient.

leapfrogs.title: H3 higher Heegner geometry -> complex L''
leapfrogs.known_baseline: Complex factorization L(E/K_D,s)=L(E,s)L(E^D,s) and nonzero L'(E^D,1) for an eligible odd twist.
leapfrogs.missing_arrow: The base-change third derivative is known to equal 3L''(E,1)L'(E^D,1), but its geometric vanishing is unknown.
leapfrogs.hypothetical_bridge: Identify a valid higher Gross–Zagier or cycle relation that forces L'''(E/K_D,1)=0 independently of assuming BSD rank equality.
leapfrogs.if_then_statement: IF L'''(E/K_D,1)=0 is proved geometrically and L'(E^D,1)≠0 is certified, THEN L''(E,1)=0.
leapfrogs.would_unlock: A single quadratic field could suffice, potentially bypassing a direct complex zero certificate.
leapfrogs.unverified_dependencies: The geometric third-derivative formula is missing; the twist nonvanishing for D=-7 is a provisional computational certificate.
leapfrogs.negative_control: When the twist derivative vanishes, product-third-derivative zero does not imply L''=0; implemented polynomial negative control. First base-change derivative is already zero for both order-two and order-four original germs with an odd twist, hence classical first-derivative Heegner height vanishing is not a cubic-order certificate.
leapfrogs.next_decisive_test: Verify the precise derivative ORDER in proposed higher Gross–Zagier and generalized Heegner-cycle literature. The 2024 Lilienfeldt–Shnidman and 2026 Du–Peng work treats central FIRST derivatives in higher WEIGHTS, not a cubic derivative for our weight-two quadratic base change. Seek a genuine third-derivative formula or park implementation.
leapfrogs.kill_criterion: Stop if varying D only restates the analytic factorization with no new theorem or cycle.
leapfrogs.not_unlocked: No demonstrated theorem establishing L''(E,1)=0, analytic rank four, Sha finiteness, or the full BSD leading coefficient.

leapfrogs.title: H4 modular-symbol congruences -> complex L''
leapfrogs.known_baseline: Exact finite congruences of Mazur–Tate elements and modular symbol data. The BKS Mazur–Tate 2025 arXiv-v1 Theorem 1.1 assumes BSD and generalized Perrin–Riou; its unconditional Corollary 1.2 applies to analytic rank one, unlike our rank-four curve.
leapfrogs.missing_arrow: Any finite p-adic congruence alone is compatible with a nonzero complex analytic invariant.
leapfrogs.hypothetical_bridge: A proven comparison must connect an algebraic projective family of modular-symbol classes with a complex Taylor coefficient.
leapfrogs.if_then_statement: IF a compatible infinite system with an independently proved comparison forces the complex L'' to zero, THEN order is at least four.
leapfrogs.would_unlock: Exact symbolic cancellation in a different arithmetic realization could bypass floating point zeros.
leapfrogs.unverified_dependencies: No map from these finite congruences to complex L'' is established; shared period normalizations are delicate.
leapfrogs.negative_control: The integer 11^m is nonzero despite vanishing modulo 11^m; a finite congruence cannot prove an exact zero. The theorem-eligibility script must reject E at rank four for the rank-one supersingular corollary and reject unknown BSD/PR hypotheses for the main theorem.
leapfrogs.next_decisive_test: Identify a single algebraic derived element and one theorem specifying its interpolation to the complex L-series.
leapfrogs.kill_criterion: Kill if the result concerns only a p-adic invariant unrelated to the target complex derivative. Reject any application of BKS 2025 Theorem 1.1 as a proof of BSD: BSD appears as explicit condition (d). For degree-11 cyclotomic Q1 its field conductor 121 also violates squarefree condition (a).
leapfrogs.not_unlocked: No demonstrated theorem establishing L''(E,1)=0, analytic rank four, Sha finiteness, or the full BSD leading coefficient.

leapfrogs.title: H5 precision-lab diagnostic -> exact vanishing mechanism
leapfrogs.known_baseline: PARI reports L'' numerically close to zero for the rank-four curve and nonzero on rank-two control 389a1.
leapfrogs.missing_arrow: Numerical near-zero values at any finite precision do not certify exact L''=0.
leapfrogs.hypothetical_bridge: Find an independently justified symbolic identity or rigidity principle, not just a smaller residual.
leapfrogs.if_then_statement: IF a concrete exact cancellation identity is proved, THEN it may certify the desired vanishing; no such identity identified.
leapfrogs.would_unlock: A cheap diagnostic can falsify wrong normalizations and route attention toward promising geometric mechanisms.
leapfrogs.unverified_dependencies: This is presently an instrumentation track, not a leapfrog conjecture with a constructed map.
leapfrogs.negative_control: Rank-two controls can have even functional equation yet nonzero L'', defeating root-sign-only explanations.
leapfrogs.next_decisive_test: Independently corroborate the derivative computations using different libraries and monitor benchmark controls.
leapfrogs.kill_criterion: Stop increasing precision if no exact symbolic or geometric mechanism emerges.
leapfrogs.not_unlocked: No demonstrated theorem establishing L''(E,1)=0, analytic rank four, Sha finiteness, or the full BSD leading coefficient.
